European football returned to Amsterdam on July 30, 2026 , as Ajax faced off against Vojvodina in a highly anticipated UEFA Europa Conference League clash. Both sides sought to establish dominance in a match that promised tactical depth and moments of individual brilliance. A Tense Opening Exchange The contest began with a cagey atmosphere as both teams looked for an opening. It was the visitors who struck first in the 40th minute; Djordje Crnomarkovic found the net following a clever assist from Lazar Randjelovic , leaving the home crowd momentarily silenced. However, Ajax showed their resilience immediately. Just a minute before the break, Davy Klaassen restored parity in the 44th minute, converting a chance set up by Youri Regeer to ensure the sides went into halftime level. The Oscar Gloukh Show The second half saw the momentum shift drastically as Oscar Gloukh took center stage. In the 53rd minute, Gloukh clinical finishing put Ajax ahead for the first time, assisted by Mika Godts . He didn't stop there, doubling his tally in the 58th minute after being played through by Steven Berghuis . The Serbian side attempted to regain composure with multiple substitutions, but the Dutch giants were in full flow, dictating the tempo across every sector of the pitch. Completing the Hat-trick The night was truly defined by Gloukh’s clinical nature. In the 71st minute, he completed a spectacular hat-trick, this time aided by an assist from substitute Oliver Edvardsen . Following his third goal, Gloukh was given a well-deserved rest, replaced by Abdellah Ouazane . Despite late yellow cards for Vojvodina's Stefan Mitrovic and Milan Kolarevic , Ajax remained composed to see out the match and secure a convincing victory on the European stage.

This encounter, filled with tactical shifts and disciplinary flashpoints, tested the resolve of both sides in their pursuit of European progress. Copenhagen Strike First from the Spot FC Copenhagen started the match with clear intent, dominating possession and forcing the visitors onto the back foot. The breakthrough arrived in the 27th minute when the referee pointed to the penalty spot. Mohamed Elyounoussi stepped up and confidently struck the ball down the middle with his right foot. Polissya goalkeeper Georgiy Bushchan committed early to his left, leaving the net exposed for the opening goal. The goal sparked a reaction from the visitors, though it was largely characterized by defensive frustration, leading to a yellow card for Oleksandr Nazarenko . Despite the tension, the Danish giants maintained their composure to head into the halftime break with a slender lead, having successfully neutralized the Ukrainian threat. Junnosuke Suzuki was shown a straight red card in the 47th minute for a professional foul as the last man, leaving FC Copenhagen to play almost the entire second period with ten men. However, the disadvantage seemed to galvanize the hosts. In the 61st minute, Mads Emil Madsen turned provider, delivering a precise ball for Robert , who made no mistake with a simple tap-in to double the lead. As the game progressed, the atmosphere grew increasingly heated. Thomas Delaney received a yellow card for dissent as the hosts looked to manage the clock. A flurry of tactical substitutions followed, with Polissya introducing Mykola Gayduchyk and Oleksandr Filippov to capitalize on their numerical superiority. Late Scare in Stoppage Time With the match entering its final moments, Polissya threw everything forward. Their persistence finally paid off in the third minute of stoppage time (90+3') when Mykola Gayduchyk found space to fire home with his right foot. The late goal set up a frantic final sixty seconds, but the FC Copenhagen defense held firm until the final whistle blew, securing a hard-fought victory despite the numerical disadvantage for much of the second half.

First Half Misfortune The opening period was largely a tactical stalemate, with clear-cut chances at a premium as both defenses remained organized. However, the deadlock was broken in a cruel fashion for the home side in the 41st minute. Gabor Vas accidentally diverted the ball into his own net, gifting Panathinaikos a 1-0 lead just before the halftime whistle blew, leaving the home fans in stunned silence. Valencia Strikes as Tensions Rise Returning for the second half, the intensity ramped up significantly. Facing a two-goal deficit, Paksi SE manager opted for a triple substitution, bringing on the likes of Daniel Bode to spark a revival. Kevin Horvath , another second-half introduction, found Daniel Bode , who made no mistake in slotting the ball home to make it 1-2. The final twenty minutes were a frantic affair as the Hungarian side pushed for an equalizer. Despite a late booking for Pavlos Pantelidis and five minutes of stoppage time, the Greek visitors held firm to see out a tense victory.
